notes: Dev ABox revision on first_proved_by (functional, inverse first_proved, subproperty proved_by): a theorem has one first complete proof, where proved_by is not functional. Related is the functional exclusion 'Is Andrew Wiles the mathematician who first proved Fermat's Last Theorem?' (alt derivation inverse; a genuine inverse question is not available because what Perelman first proved has two answers after the edit). Derived: a composition about Perelman (the Fields Medal he declined; Wiles was never offered one), a binding through the older name 'Fermat's conjecture', and the subproperty first_proved_by ⊑ proved_by composed with Perelman's proof of the Poincaré conjecture (yes/no). Caveat: 'Fermat's conjecture' is a rare alias and also names the claim that Fermat numbers are prime, so the binding relies on the check catching models without the alias. Mathematics has no consistent world after an edit, so everything is determinate. Unrelated near asks the book in whose margin Fermat wrote the theorem (Arithmetica), untouched by the edit. New evidence is Wikipedia quotes and search counts (infini-gram was blocked on 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12); earlier Dolma counts are kept.
